note: Routes that cannot be driven by any gauntlet tier today. Every entry names WHY and WHO. A route with no entry and no observation appears in the report's 'NO stated reason at all' row, which is the row that should make someone uncomfortable. blocked.reason: Dealer accelerator, not part of the seven-role successor release set; no tier deploys it. THE FRAME-CLEANLINESS HALF OF THIS ROW IS RESOLVED (W2h, 2026-08-27): measured at c3c4950 and again at 5e25f8e, cargo build-sbf on programs/dclutch-dealer-accelerator-sbf emits ZERO 'overwrites values in the frame' diagnostics, against 253 measured on the same tree at the immediately preceding HEAD. TA-DLR's root cause was correct and is independent of the fix: with `no-entrypoint` set, dclutch-trading-sbf compiles without its own #[global_allocator], which leaves __rust_alloc an opaque extern that cannot be folded at its call sites and spills hot_v3::process_hot_execution_v3 past the SBPF v0 4,096-byte frame. What changed is the headroom, not the allocator: process_hot_execution_v3 used 3,904 bytes of that frame with the outgoing-argument area filling the rest, and c3c4950 split it into an authentication half (3,008 bytes) and an execution half (2,496), which absorbs the opaque extern. TA-DLR's two-edit patch is therefore NOT required for this row and is NOT applied. It remains the principled fix for the underlying incoherence -- a no-entrypoint library build of Trading still runs Hot code under whichever allocator its host executable installs, not the one the shipped Trading program uses -- and if it is taken: re-measure on top of c3c4950 rather than against the stale 253; land both halves together (either alone is a duplicate or a missing #[global_allocator], both hard errors); and per W1f keep admit_heap_frame_v1 and lift_declared_heap_profile_v1 reachable in the SHIPPED ELF, where DCLTPCB1 depends on them on chain now. Widening the cfg does not move the shipped build either way, since `no-entrypoint` is off there and both predicates already evaluate the same. The emitted accelerator .so was never contaminated in any case: process_hot_execution_v3 is dead-stripped from it.
blocked.owner: TA-DLR (the campaign); frame blocker cleared by W2h, the allocator-coherence question is an owner decision

Consent still needs the PREDECESSOR release's bound upgrade authority to sign, so a cohort revoking authority on both infrastructure roles is permanently unfoundable -- 6155219a refuses that at plan time by name. blocked.reason: STRUCTURALLY UNDRIVABLE, and the emptiness is convicted rather than asserted. This is the `Some((recovery_id, policy))` arm -- the recovery-BEARING half of `authenticate_recovery_policy` -- and its satisfying set is empty for three independent reasons, any one of which suffices. (1) `recovery_walk_has_a_live_route` (programs/dclutch-core-sbf/src/resolution.rs:883) returns FALSE for `CreateFund`, so a Market whose SourceMaterialV3 names a recovery policy refuses fund creation with `CoreSbfError::RecoveryWalkUnavailable` (0x3011, lib.rs:160) at resolution.rs:726, before the arm's body runs. (2) The two actions the predicate DOES admit, `VerifyFundReady` and `CloseFund`, each require a fund that `CreateFund` refused to create, so neither can ever present recovery-bearing material. (3) `CloseFund` is separately refused at the top of `resolution::process` (line 136), so it cannot reach the call at all. The weld is doubled off-chain: `build_resolution_create_fund_v3` returns `ResolutionCoreOperatorErrorV3::RecoveryWalkUnavailable` for exactly this shape (crates/dclutch-resolution-core-v3-operator/src/lib.rs:1131), so the instruction cannot even be built. The stated cause is a real protocol fact and not a gap in the harness: `SourceResolutionStateV2` HAS NO TRANSITION THAT ADVANCES A RECOVERY ATTEMPT -- `funded.rs` plans the whole failure walk as Primary -> Exhausted -> FailureCommitted -- so a fund created over recovery-bearing material would have no terminal at all. A fixture that faked the precondition would witness nothing. THE POSITIVE CONTROL that this is a branch problem and not an unreached guard: the sibling arm `core/authenticate_no_recovery_entries#None` is EXECUTED (resolution-core-v3-programtest, one CreateFund at 286,481 CU) -- the guard is reached and evaluated on every fund creation; it is the other branch that has no inhabitant.
